content.text:
<permissions instructions>
Sandbox: the workspace is writable, the network is off. Commands that need more ask the developer first, with a one-line justification.
</permissions instructions>

<collaboration_mode>
Work without stopping for confirmation on read-only steps. Stop and ask before anything that changes files outside the workspace.
</collaboration_mode>
Add a --done flag to `tasky list` that shows only finished tasks.

summary.text: First look at how the list command parses flags.

request_body.instructions:
You work as a coding agent in a terminal on the developer's machine, inside the tasky repository.
Read before you write: open the files a change touches, and check how similar code is already done.
Make focused edits with apply_patch if the tool exists; never rewrite a whole file to change a line.
Run commands with exec_command. Prefer fast, read-only commands while exploring.
After an edit, run go build and the tests for the package you changed, and fix what you broke.
Keep the final message short: what changed, where, and anything the developer still has to decide.
Do not run commands that delete data or rewrite history unless the developer asked for exactly that.
If the request is unclear, ask one precise question instead of guessing at a large change.

tools.description: Runs a shell command and returns its output, or a process handle if it is still running after wait_ms.
tools.name: exec_command

directory.description: Directory to run it in; defaults to the workspace.

escalation.description: Ask for more than the sandbox allows.

output_cap.description: Truncate output beyond this many tokens.

pty.description: Allocate a terminal so interactive programs work.

rationale.description: Why escalation is needed, shown to the developer.

remember_prefix.description: Command prefix the developer may approve for the rest of the session.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for output before returning.

tools.description: Writes characters to a running command session and returns new output.
tools.name: send_input

keys.description: Characters to write; may be empty to just poll.

output_cap.description: Truncate output beyond this many tokens.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for output.

tools.description: Asks the developer up to three short questions with suggested answers.
tools.name: ask_user

tools.description: Edits files with a patch in the grammar below. Paths are relative to the workspace.

format.definition:
start: "*** Begin Patch" NL section+ "*** End Patch" NL?
section: added | removed | changed
added: "*** Add File: " PATH NL plus_line+
removed: "*** Delete File: " PATH NL
changed: "*** Update File: " PATH NL rename? chunk+
rename: "*** Move to: " PATH NL
chunk: "@@" TEXT? NL diff_line+
plus_line: "+" TEXT NL
diff_line: (" " | "+" | "-") TEXT NL
PATH: /[^\r\n]+/
TEXT: /[^\r\n]*/
NL: /\r?\n/

tools.name: apply_patch

tools.description: Attaches a local image file so the model can look at it.
tools.name: show_image
